topic: First champion of the modern Olympic Games: James Brendan Connolly (USA), triple jump (hop, step and jump), Panathenaic Stadium, Athens, 6 April 1896, 13.71 m; winners in 1896 received silver medals and an olive branch (retroactively counted as gold); he withdrew from Harvard after being refused leave; travelled by German freighter to Naples; first Olympic champion since the ancient Games ended in the late 4th century AD
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: A Greek runner won the first modern Olympic title.
myths.reality: The first final decided in Athens 1896 was the triple jump on the opening day, won by American James Connolly; Spyridon Louis's marathon came on 10 April.

landscape.our_gap: 1896 Shorts retell the marathon or Coubertin; nobody asks who won the very first title, shows the jump against a bus, and draws the freighter route a dropout took to get there.

ioc_1896.title: Athens 1896 Olympic Games — results and history
ioc_1896.notes: opening day 6 April 1896; James Connolly (USA) first champion of the modern Games in the triple jump; winners received silver medals and olive branches

olympedia_connolly.title: James Connolly — athlete profile
olympedia_connolly.notes: triple jump 13.71 m, 6 April 1896, Panathenaic Stadium; left Harvard to compete; also 2nd high jump, 3rd long jump

britannica_connolly.title: James Connolly — American athlete and writer
britannica_connolly.notes: first Olympic champion of the modern era; Harvard denied leave, he withdrew; travelled by freighter to Naples then train and boat to Athens

harvard_gazette.title: The first modern Olympic champion was a Harvard dropout
harvard_gazette.notes: Connolly, a South Boston son of Irish immigrants, withdrew from Harvard in 1896 after being refused leave; Harvard later offered an honorary degree, which he declined

tfl_bus.title: New Routemaster — vehicle specification
tfl_bus.notes: the New Routemaster double-decker is 11.23 m long; Connolly's 13.71 m exceeds it

wiki_ancient.title: Ancient Olympic Games
wiki_ancient.notes: last recorded ancient Games AD 393 (traditional) — roughly 1,500 years before 1896

claims.text: James Connolly of the United States won the first title of the modern Olympics, the triple jump, in Athens on 6 April 1896.
vo: who won the first gold medal of the modern olympics
the united states. james connolly, a boston student, won the triple jump in athens on 6 april 1896

claims.text: Connolly's winning triple jump measured 13.71 m — longer than a London double-decker bus (11.23 m).
vo: he hopped, skipped and jumped nearly 14 metres, further than a london bus is long

claims.text: Harvard refused Connolly leave of absence; he withdrew and travelled to Athens by freighter via Naples.
vo: harvard refused him leave to go, so he quit, and crossed the atlantic by cargo ship to compete

claims.text: The ancient Games ended in the late 4th century AD, so 1896 crowned the first Olympic champion in roughly 1,500 years.
vo: no olympic champion had been crowned for 1,500 years, and the man who ended the wait was a dropout
